title: Edmund and the Regiment
premise: In the winter of 1813, at a riverfront workshop that quietly prints regimental muster rolls, nurse Sable Lockridge keeps a private ledger of soldiers whose names officers have struck from the record. When a boy named Edmund is abandoned at their door with orders to 'forget the face,' Sable realizes he is the illegitimate heir of a colonel whose true will — naming Edmund over his legitimate sons — is hidden inside the workshop's printing plates. As the ice on the river thaws and the colonel's family closes in to burn the evidence, Sable must choose between loyalty to the found family of printers who sheltered them and the truth the ledger demands. The book ends with the workshop half-burned but the will printed and witnessed before the ice breaks: Edmund claimed by his name, Sable's ledger entered into the record, and history no longer something that happens elsewhere.
about_author: Theo Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing regimental pay books in provincial record offices. They write historical fiction about the people paperwork was designed to erase.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Omissions
chapters.summary: Sable Lockridge, recovering from field service, takes work at the Quill & Anchor workshop, where they notice names missing from official muster rolls and begin recording them secretly. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: wary detachment — Sable insists history happens to other people, even as the ledger grows.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: On a freezing night, a boy of about seven is left at the workshop door with a note reading only 'forget the face.' The printers debate turning him over to the parish; Sable, against their own rule about attachments, feeds him. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness breaking through self-protection.

chapters.title: What Edmund Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund fragments reveal a grand house, a kind man teaching him letters, and men arguing over papers. Sable recognizes the man from a portrait plate in the workshop's stock: Colonel Ashworth, recently dead. POV: alternating Sable and Edmund. Emotional beat: dawning dread that the child is evidence someone wants erased.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Will
chapters.summary: Sable discovers the will naming Edmund as heir was entrusted to the workshop for printing but never released — suppressed by the Ashworth family, who paid the master printer to destroy it. The old printer's guilt explains his silence. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the found family.

chapters.title: Visitors from the Great House
chapters.summary: Colonel Ashworth's eldest son arrives, courteous and cold, asking after 'a stray child' and offering gold for any papers left in the colonel's care. The master printer lies badly; Sable hides Edmund in the type loft. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Names in the Ice
chapters.summary: Sable cross-references the ledger with the suppressed will and finds the colonel had also demanded restitution for soldiers cheated of pay — the omissions were theft, not clerical error. The stakes widen beyond one child. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: righteous anger fusing personal and public truth.

chapters.title: The Split
chapters.summary: The workshop votes: print the will and ruin themselves, or take the money and survive the winter. The master printer's daughter sides with Sable; the old man wavers, terrified of the family's reach. Edmund overhears everything. POV: ensemble, anchored by Edmund. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: Night Runners
chapters.summary: Ashworth's men come for Edmund before dawn; the daughter smuggles him out along the frozen towpath while Sable stays behind to misdirect them and is taken to the great house. POV: split between Sable captive and Edmund fleeing. Emotional beat: terror and sacrifice — loyalty tested in both directions.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Climax. In the great house, Sable confronts the family with the ledger itself, buying time; at the workshop, the press runs through the night printing the will and the restored names. The magistrate arrives just as the river ice cracks — witnesses sign, the son's threats collapse, and the fire set in the workshop is beaten back. POV: Sable and Edmund converging. Emotional beat: triumph purchased at real cost.

chapters.title: Every Name Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Spring. The workshop, scorched but standing, prints its first honest roll; Sable reads the recovered names aloud in the yard with Edmund beside them, now acknowledged heir and apprentice both. The ledger finds its way into the county archive. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — history has happened to them, and they kept it.
